topics.title: Agent Skills format (SKILL.md) and specification
topics.why: The portable instruction-folder format every agent in the garage loads; read the frontmatter rules before you write a SKILL.md or vendor a skill.

practices.text: name is 1-64 chars, lowercase/digits/hyphens, must equal the folder name; description is 1-1024 chars and must say what the skill does AND when to use it.
Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines (~5k tokens); move detail to references/ and scripts/ loaded on demand (progressive disclosure).
Validate with the reference library: skills-ref validate ./my-skill.

practices.text: Use Pydantic v2 models for request/response schemas and keep business logic out of route handlers.
Never run blocking I/O inside async def endpoints; use sync def (threadpool) or an async driver.

resources.name: FastAPI
resources.note: Default for Python APIs: Pydantic typing, automatic OpenAPI, dependency injection.

resources.name: Django
resources.note: Batteries included (ORM, admin, auth, migrations); Django 6.x. Best when the app is more than an API.

resources.name: Litestar

resources.name: Django Ninja

resources.name: Flask

resources.name: Echo
resources.note: Full framework (binding, validation hooks, middleware) that stays close to net/http.

resources.name: Gin
resources.note: Most popular Go framework; own context type, fast binding. Fiber (fasthttp) is faster but not net/http compatible.

resources.name: Huma
resources.note: Generates OpenAPI 3.1 from Go types on top of any router; pick when the API contract matters.

resources.name: Rocket

practices.text: Run a supported major (18 is current; each major gets 5 years) and read the release notes before upgrading.
Read the wiki's Don't Do This before designing a schema: timestamptz not timestamp, text not varchar(n), no money type, no serial in new code.

topics.why: Keep very large or time-based tables fast to query, index and purge.

practices.text: Partition only when a table is 100M+ rows or has time-based retention; include the partition key in the primary key and every unique constraint; use DETACH CONCURRENTLY to drop old data.

SQLite is the right choice for most small-to-medium sites; it is the wrong choice for many concurrent writers across hosts.

topics.title: Zero-downtime schema migrations (the rules)
topics.why: Change production schemas without locking tables or taking the app down; these are the rules every migration linter encodes.

practices.text: Always set lock_timeout (and statement_timeout) before DDL and retry on failure; a blocked ALTER queues every other query behind it.
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY; add NOT NULL via a NOT VALID check constraint then VALIDATE; add foreign keys NOT VALID then VALIDATE; never ALTER COLUMN TYPE on a big table in place.
Separate schema changes from data backfills and deploys: expand (add nullable column) -> backfill in batches -> switch code -> contract (drop old) in a later release.

resources.name: pg-schema-diff (Stripe)
resources.note: Go library/CLI producing safe, concurrent-index migrations from a schema diff; migra is deprecated, Supabase CLI now uses pg-delta.

resources.name: pg-osc
resources.note: Online schema change for big Postgres tables (shadow table + triggers), gh-ost style.

resources.name: Reshape
resources.note: Earlier zero-downtime migration tool with the same schema-view approach as pgroll.

topics.title: Indexing strategy and index advisors
topics.why: Add the right indexes (and only those) for real query patterns, and find missing or unused ones.

practices.text: Index for the WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY columns of real slow queries (pg_stat_statements), create CONCURRENTLY, use composite indexes in filter-then-sort order, and drop unused indexes (pg_stat_user_indexes).
Choose the index type: B-tree default, GIN for jsonb/arrays/full-text, GiST for ranges/geometry, BRIN for huge append-only tables, HNSW for vectors.

resources.name: Use The Index, Luke
resources.note: Free book on SQL indexing for developers (Postgres, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server); the canonical explanation.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Indexes
resources.note: Index types, multicolumn, partial, expression and covering indexes, CONCURRENTLY builds.

resources.name: Supabase - Managing indexes
resources.note: Practical, example-led walkthrough of index types and when to use them.

resources.name: Dexter
resources.note: Automatic index suggestions from pg_stat_statements using HypoPG hypothetical indexes.

resources.name: HypoPG
resources.note: Test whether an index would be used before building it (PostgreSQL licence); supabase/index_advisor wraps it as a SQL function.

topics.title: Reading query plans (EXPLAIN)
topics.why: Diagnose slow queries by reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE output correctly.

practices.text: Use EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT TEXT) on production-like data; look for row-estimate mismatches, Seq Scans on big tables, Sort/Hash spills to disk and nested loops with high loop counts.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Using EXPLAIN
resources.note: Official walkthrough of plan nodes, costs and ANALYZE output.

resources.name: pev2 (explain.dalibo.com)
resources.note: Plan visualiser; embeddable component or the hosted explain.dalibo.com.

resources.name: explain.depesz.com
resources.note: Text-plan analyser highlighting the most expensive nodes; anonymisation option.

resources.name: pganalyze - Basics of Postgres query planning
resources.note: Readable guide to plan nodes plus an EXPLAIN glossary.

resources.name: PostgreSQL wiki - Slow Query Questions
resources.note: What to collect before asking for help (or before an agent starts guessing); pg_hint_plan exists for forcing plans as a last resort.

topics.title: Transactions and isolation levels
topics.why: Pick the isolation level that actually prevents the anomaly you care about, and handle serialization failures.

practices.text: Postgres default READ COMMITTED allows lost updates and write skew; use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or SERIALIZABLE with retry for check-then-write logic; keep transactions short.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Transaction Isolation
resources.note: Exact anomaly table and SSI behaviour for Postgres.

resources.name: Hermitage
resources.note: Kleppmann's test suite showing which anomalies each database's isolation levels really prevent.

resources.name: Hermitage - Testing the I in ACID
resources.note: Companion article explaining the anomalies in plain language.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - MVCC introduction
resources.note: Chapter covering concurrency control, locking and serialization failure handling.

resources.name: Jepsen analyses
resources.note: Independent consistency tests of real databases; read before trusting a vendor's isolation claims.

topics.title: Locking and lock monitoring
topics.why: Understand which statements take which locks, detect blocking chains and avoid deadlocks.

practices.text: Acquire locks in a consistent order, keep DDL and long transactions apart, set lock_timeout, and use advisory locks for application-level mutual exclusion.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Explicit Locking
resources.note: Lock modes, conflict matrix, row locks, deadlocks and advisory locks.

resources.name: pglocks.org
resources.note: Interactive table of which lock every SQL command takes and what it conflicts with.

resources.name: PostgreSQL wiki - Lock Monitoring
resources.note: Ready queries over pg_locks/pg_stat_activity to find blockers and blocked sessions.

resources.name: Postgres lock trees (postgres.ai)
resources.note: Query that renders the blocking tree with pg_blocking_pids.

resources.name: eugene
resources.note: Shows the locks a migration takes; see also squawk.

topics.title: Connection pooling
topics.why: Keep Postgres connection counts low and stable in front of many app instances or serverless functions.

practices.text: Size the app pool to a few connections per CPU core of the database, use transaction pooling for stateless apps, and avoid session-level features (prepared statements by name, SET, advisory locks) behind a transaction pooler.

resources.name: PgBouncer
resources.note: The standard lightweight pooler (ISC); config reference at pgbouncer.org/config.html; single-threaded, run several if needed.

resources.name: How to Manage Connections Efficiently in Postgres (Brandur)
resources.note: Why connections are expensive and how to combine app pools with PgBouncer.

resources.name: PgDog
resources.note: Rust pooler with load balancing and sharding (2025+); AGPL, run as a service. PgCat is its less active predecessor.

resources.name: Supavisor
resources.note: Elixir multi-tenant pooler built for serverless connection storms (Supabase).

resources.name: Odyssey
resources.note: Multi-threaded pooler from Yandex for very high connection counts.

topics.title: Backups and point-in-time recovery
topics.why: Be able to restore any Postgres or SQLite database to a point in time, and prove it regularly.

practices.text: pg_dump is not a backup strategy for PITR: use base backups + WAL archiving to object storage, encrypt, keep retention, and run automated restore tests.

resources.name: pgBackRest
resources.note: Parallel, incremental, encrypted backups with S3/Azure/GCS repos and PITR (MIT); user guide at pgbackrest.org.

resources.name: WAL-G
resources.note: Fast WAL archiving and base backups to object storage (Apache-2.0); also MySQL/MongoDB.

resources.name: Barman
resources.note: Backup manager with catalogue and retention policies; used by CloudNativePG.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Continuous Archiving and PITR
resources.note: How WAL archiving and recovery targets work underneath every tool.

resources.name: PG Back Web
resources.note: Web UI scheduling pg_dump backups to S3 with restore; good enough for small home-server databases. SQLite: Litestream.

topics.title: Replication and high availability
topics.why: Run streaming/logical replication and automatic failover without hand-rolled scripts.

resources.name: Patroni

resources.note: Publications/subscriptions for selective replication, CDC and near-zero-downtime major upgrades; watch replication slot disk growth.

resources.name: Autobase

resources.name: pg_auto_failover

resources.name: repmgr
resources.note: Older replication manager (GPL); prefer Patroni for new clusters.

topics.title: Row-level security, roles and privileges
topics.why: Enforce tenant and user data isolation in the database and give each app component least-privilege roles.

practices.text: Use separate roles for migrations (owner), the app (DML only) and read-only analytics; never connect the app as a superuser.
RLS policies must use indexed columns, wrap function calls like auth.uid() in (select ...) so they are evaluated once, and be tested with SET ROLE for each role.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Row Security Policies
resources.note: ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY semantics, USING vs WITH CHECK, bypass rules.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - CREATE POLICY
resources.note: Policy syntax, permissive vs restrictive policies, per-command policies.

resources.name: Supabase - Row Level Security guide
resources.note: Practical patterns and performance tips (indexes, select wrapping, security definer helpers) that apply to any Postgres.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Privileges
resources.note: GRANT/REVOKE, default privileges and ownership; pair with the role attributes page.

resources.name: Supabase Postgres best-practices skill
resources.note: Agent skill with RLS, security and schema rules for Postgres anywhere.

topics.title: Data modelling, types and constraints
topics.why: Design normalised schemas with the right Postgres types and constraints so the database guards the invariants.

practices.text: Normalise to 3NF by default, denormalise only with evidence; put every invariant you can into NOT NULL, CHECK, UNIQUE and FK constraints; use text, timestamptz, numeric, jsonb (sparingly) and bigint/uuid keys.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Data Types
resources.note: Every built-in type; read before picking varchar(n) or float for money.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Constraints
resources.note: CHECK, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PK, FK and EXCLUDE constraints with deferrable semantics.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - JSON Types
resources.note: jsonb operators and indexing; use for genuinely variable attributes, not as a schema escape hatch.

resources.name: PostgreSQL wiki - Don't Do This
resources.note: Type and schema anti-patterns to avoid.

resources.name: pg-aiguide - design-postgres-tables skill
resources.note: Agent skill encoding table-design rules (keys, types, constraints, naming) with references.

topics.title: Soft deletes, audit trails and history tables
topics.why: Decide how to delete and how to keep a record of changes without polluting every query.

practices.text: Prefer hard deletes plus a deleted_records archive table (or temporal history) over deleted_at columns that every query must remember to filter; if you soft-delete, enforce it with views or ORM default scopes and partial unique indexes.

resources.name: Soft Deletion Probably Isn't Worth It (Brandur)
resources.note: The argument against deleted_at and the archive-table alternative.

resources.name: pgaudit
resources.note: Session/object audit logging to the Postgres log (PostgreSQL licence); compliance-grade, no tables.

resources.name: temporal_tables
resources.note: System-period versioning (history table per table) via trigger; a pure plpgsql version exists for managed Postgres.

resources.name: pgMemento
resources.note: Row-level audit trail with schema versioning stored as jsonb.

resources.name: audit-trigger (2ndQuadrant)
resources.note: Classic generic trigger-based audit table (PostgreSQL licence); finished, copy and adapt. supa_audit is archived.

topics.title: Primary keys and identifiers (UUIDv7, ULID, TypeID)
topics.why: Pick key types that are sortable, index-friendly and safe to expose.

practices.text: Use bigint identity for internal keys or UUIDv7 (time-ordered) for distributed/exposed keys; avoid random UUIDv4 primary keys on large tables (index fragmentation) and never expose sequential ids publicly.

resources.name: RFC 9562 - UUIDs
resources.note: Defines UUIDv6/v7/v8; v7 is the one to use for new keys.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - UUID functions
resources.note: uuidv7() is built in since PostgreSQL 18; fboulnois/pg_uuidv7 extension for older versions.

resources.name: TypeID
resources.note: Stripe-style prefixed, K-sortable ids on UUIDv7 (user_2x4y6z...) with implementations in many languages; ULID (oklog/ulid, ulid/javascript) is the older alternative.

resources.name: nanoid
resources.note: Short URL-safe random ids for slugs/tokens (not sortable); ports in every language. UUID libs: uuidjs/uuid, google/uuid, uuid-rs/uuid, uuid-utils (Python).

topics.title: Money, decimals, dates and time zones
topics.why: Store and compute money and time without floating-point or time-zone bugs.

practices.text: Store money as integer minor units or numeric(19,4) with an explicit currency column; never float/double or the Postgres money type.
Store instants as timestamptz in UTC, store the IANA zone name separately for user-facing times, and store future local events as local time + zone (rules change).

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Numeric Types
resources.note: numeric vs float semantics and precision.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Date/Time Types
resources.note: timestamptz behaviour, intervals and time-zone handling.

resources.name: Dinero.js

resources.name: Falsehoods programmers believe (awesome-falsehood)
resources.note: Time, dates, names, addresses, prices: read the time section before modelling; use Temporal/jiff/java.time style APIs, not Date arithmetic.

practices.text: Every migration PR shows the SQL, the lock it takes, the estimated runtime on production-size data and the rollback plan.

topics.title: Database testing and ephemeral databases
topics.why: Run tests against a real database quickly and in isolation, in CI and locally.

practices.text: Test against the real engine (container or PGlite), use one template database cloned per test or transactional rollback, and run migrations in CI from an empty database.

topics.why: Fill dev/test databases with realistic data and produce safe copies of production.

resources.name: PostgreSQL Anonymizer
resources.note: Extension declaring masking rules in the schema (static, dynamic or dump-time masking); lives on GitLab.

topics.title: Performance monitoring and configuration tuning
topics.why: See which queries cost the most and set the handful of Postgres settings that matter for the hardware.

practices.text: Enable pg_stat_statements everywhere, review top queries by total_exec_time weekly, and start config from PGTune values (shared_buffers ~25% RAM, effective_cache_size, work_mem per sort, random_page_cost 1.1 on SSD).

resources.name: pg_stat_statements docs
resources.note: The one extension to always enable; normalised query stats.

resources.name: PgHero
resources.note: Dashboard for slow queries, unused/duplicate indexes, bloat and connections; Docker image available.

resources.name: pgwatch
resources.note: Metrics collector with Grafana dashboards; postgres_exporter is the Prometheus-native route. pgbadger analyses logs.

resources.note: Starting postgresql.conf from RAM/CPU/workload (hosted at pgtune.leopard.in.ua); timescaledb-tune for Timescale.

resources.name: postgresqlco.nf
resources.note: Every configuration parameter explained with recommendations; postgres_dba gives ready psql reports.

topics.title: Vacuum, bloat and major-version upgrades
topics.why: Keep tables and indexes healthy and move between Postgres majors with minimal downtime.

practices.text: Tune autovacuum per large table (lower scale factors), monitor bloat and dead tuples, use pg_repack rather than VACUUM FULL, and reindex CONCURRENTLY after big deletes.
Upgrade with pg_upgrade --link for minutes of downtime or logical replication for near-zero; run ANALYZE after and test extensions first.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Routine Vacuuming
resources.note: Why vacuum exists (MVCC, wraparound) and autovacuum tuning parameters.

resources.name: pg_repack

resources.name: pgsql-bloat-estimation

resources.name: pgautoupgrade Docker image
resources.note: Drop-in Postgres image that runs pg_upgrade on start; why-upgrade.depesz.com lists what changes between versions.

topics.title: Bulk loading and large data operations
topics.why: Load millions of rows or migrate from another database fast without wrecking production performance.

practices.text: Use COPY (not INSERT loops), load in batches of thousands with periodic commits, drop/recreate indexes and FKs for initial loads, raise maintenance_work_mem, and ANALYZE afterwards.

resources.name: PostgreSQL docs - Populating a Database
resources.note: The official bulk-load checklist.

resources.name: pg_bulkload

practices.text: Default to Polars (lazy API) or DuckDB for new code; keep pandas for library compatibility; exchange data as Arrow/Parquet rather than CSV.

topics.title: Database MCP servers (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB)

resources.name: Postgres MCP Pro
resources.note: EXPLAIN, index tuning, health checks; --access-mode=restricted for read-only; needs DATABASE_URI (network, DB creds).

resources.name: DBHub
resources.note: Postgres/MySQL/MariaDB/SQL Server/SQLite in one token-light server; read-only mode, row limit, query timeout; needs DSN.

resources.name: MongoDB MCP Server
resources.note: Official; readOnly option; connection string or Atlas API creds.

resources.name: ClickHouse MCP
resources.note: Official, read-only by default, also runs chDB locally. Other official servers: redis/mcp-redis (use a read-only ACL user), motherduckdb/mcp-server-motherduck (DuckDB files), qdrant/mcp-server-qdrant, elastic/mcp-server-elasticsearch, supabase/mcp and neondatabase/mcp-server-neon (dev only). topics.title: Framework MCP servers and agent toolkits
topics.why: Give agents runtime insight into the app framework (routes, schema, logs, docs) and let them wrap APIs as tools.

resources.name: Context7
resources.note: Up-to-date docs for any library pulled into context; remote service (network, API key recommended).

resources.name: FastMCP
resources.note: Python framework for MCP servers; FastMCP.from_openapi()/from_fastapi() exposes any existing API to agents in a few lines.

topics.title: Reference algorithm implementations per language
topics.why: Copy a known-correct, readable implementation of a classic algorithm into a project instead of re-deriving it.

practices.text: Before copying, run or read the repo's tests for that algorithm; collections accept community PRs of uneven quality.

resources.name: TheAlgorithms/Python
resources.note: Largest per-language collection; MIT. Check tests before copying, quality varies by folder.

resources.name: TheAlgorithms/Java
resources.note: Same project for Java; MIT.

resources.name: TheAlgorithms/Rust
resources.note: Rust edition; MIT, idiomatic and tested.

resources.name: TheAlgorithms/C-Plus-Plus
resources.note: C++ edition; MIT. The C and JavaScript editions are GPL-3.0 (reference only).

resources.name: javascript-algorithms (trekhleb)
resources.note: Best JS/TS collection with explanations and tests; MIT. Prefer over TheAlgorithms/JavaScript (GPL).

topics.title: Competitive-programming libraries (cp-algorithms, KACTL, AC Library)
topics.why: Grab compact, battle-tested implementations of advanced algorithms (segment trees, flows, FFT, suffix arrays) with complexity notes.

resources.name: cp-algorithms
resources.note: Translated e-maxx; the canonical explanation + code for ~200 algorithms. CC-BY-SA-4.0: read, don't paste verbatim into permissive projects.

resources.name: KACTL
resources.note: KTH team notebook (C++): dense, verified snippets with complexity headers. No LICENSE file in repo root; treat as reference.

resources.name: AtCoder Library (ACL)
resources.note: CC0 C++ library: segtree, lazysegtree, fenwick, dsu, maxflow, mincostflow, convolution, math. Safest to vendor.

resources.name: codelibrary (indy256)
resources.note: Unlicense; algorithms in C++, Java, Kotlin, Python, Rust. Good when ACL lacks a language.

resources.name: PyRival
resources.note: Apache-2.0 Python CP library (fast IO, graphs, number theory, strings).

topics.title: Polyglot task implementations (Rosetta Code)
topics.why: See how one task is idiomatically solved across many languages when porting code or picking an approach.

resources.name: Rosetta Code
resources.note: 1,200+ tasks in hundreds of languages; GFDL 1.3 content, use for understanding not pasting.

resources.name: RosettaCodeData mirror
resources.note: Git mirror of all Rosetta solutions as files; handy for grep. No licence file beyond upstream GFDL.

resources.name: algorithms (keon, Python)
resources.note: MIT minimal Python implementations with pytest coverage; smaller and cleaner than TheAlgorithms.

topics.title: Graph algorithms and shortest paths
topics.why: Traverse, analyse and route over graphs: BFS/DFS, Dijkstra, A*, flows, components, topological sort.

resources.name: NetworkX
resources.note: Python graph library with every classic algorithm; BSD-3. Not for very large graphs.

resources.name: petgraph
resources.note: Rust graph data structures + algorithms (Dijkstra, A*, SCC, toposort). MIT/Apache-2.0 dual.

resources.name: gonum/graph
resources.note: Go: graph package inside gonum (paths, flow, community). BSD-3.

resources.name: Red Blob Games: A* introduction

resources.name: cp-algorithms: graphs
resources.note: Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Floyd, SCC, bridges, flows, matching with proofs and code. JGraphT (EPL) and RoutingKit (BSD) for Java/road networks.

resources.note: Intro plus classic problems (knapsack, LCS, divide-and-conquer DP, SOS DP).

resources.name: NeetCode roadmap (DP sections)

resources.name: Competitive Programmer's Handbook (cphb)
resources.note: Free PDF; chapter 7 is a compact DP treatment. CC BY-NC-SA: read only.

topics.title: String algorithms: tries, Aho-Corasick, suffix arrays/automata
topics.why: Multi-pattern search, prefix dictionaries, substring queries and finite-state lookup tables.

resources.name: cp-algorithms: strings
resources.note: KMP/prefix function, Z, hashing, suffix array/automaton, Aho-Corasick with code.

resources.name: pyahocorasick
resources.note: C-backed Aho-Corasick trie for Python; BSD-3.

resources.name: fst (Rust)
resources.note: Finite state transducers for huge ordered sets/maps with fuzzy and range queries. Stable since 2024 (finished).

resources.name: libdivsufsort
resources.note: Reference suffix-array construction in C; MIT, finished classic (last change 2020).

topics.title: String similarity, fuzzy matching and diff

resources.note: Python/C++ fuzzy matching, MIT; drop-in replacement for fuzzywuzzy (GPL).

resources.name: strsim-rs
resources.note: Rust string distance metrics (Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, Sørensen-Dice).

resources.name: jsdiff
resources.note: JS text diff (chars/words/lines/JSON) and unified patches; BSD-3.

resources.name: similar (Rust)
resources.note: Myers/patience diff with inline highlighting; used by insta.

resources.name: go-diff
resources.note: Go port of diff-match-patch. Google's original diff-match-patch repo is archived (2024).

topics.title: Computational geometry and spatial indexes

resources.name: Shapely
resources.note: Python planar geometry on GEOS; BSD-3.

resources.name: geo (georust)
resources.note: Rust geometry primitives and algorithms; MIT/Apache-2.0. Pair with rstar for R-trees.

resources.name: Turf.js
resources.note: Modular JS geospatial analysis (GeoJSON); MIT.

resources.name: RBush / Flatbush
resources.note: Fast JS R-tree (RBush) and static packed R-tree (Flatbush, ISC) for 2-D box queries.

resources.name: H3
resources.note: Hexagonal hierarchical geospatial index with bindings for most languages; Apache-2.0. S2 (google/s2geometry) is the spherical alternative. CGAL is GPL/LGPL: reference only.

topics.title: Number theory and modular arithmetic

resources.note: Primality, factorisation, Euler phi, modular inverse, CRT, discrete log, FFT/NTT.

resources.name: primesieve

resources.name: AtCoder Library: math
resources.note: CC0 pow_mod, inv_mod, crt, floor_sum, convolution (NTT).

resources.name: AtCoder Library: dsu
resources.note: CC0 C++ dsu.hpp (~60 lines) — copy it.

resources.name: williamfiset/Algorithms: UnionFind

resources.name: cp-algorithms: Fenwick tree
resources.note: Binary indexed tree with range update tricks.

resources.name: AtCoder Library: segtree / lazysegtree / fenwicktree
resources.note: CC0 generic C++ templates; documented in document_en/.

resources.name: williamfiset/Algorithms: priority queues
resources.note: Indexed d-ary heap with decrease-key (Java, MIT).

resources.name: aHash

resources.name: Abseil containers (flat_hash_map)
resources.note: Google's SwissTable C++ maps and the design talk linked in docs.

resources.note: Go Bloom filter with sizing helpers; BSD-2.

resources.name: axiomhq/hyperloglog
resources.note: Go HLL++ with sparse representation and loglog-beta bias correction.

resources.name: datasketch

resources.name: t-digest

resources.name: Apache DataSketches
resources.note: Production sketch library (Theta, HLL, KLL quantiles, frequent items) with C++/Python ports.

resources.name: mailgun/groupcache

resources.name: lafikl/consistent
resources.note: Ring + bounded-load variant in Go; unchanged since 2023.

topics.title: Retries, backoff, jitter and idempotency keys
topics.why: Make clients and APIs safe to retry: exponential backoff with jitter, retry budgets, idempotency keys.

practices.text: Add jitter to every exponential backoff; synchronised retries are what turn a blip into an outage.
Cap retries with a budget (e.g. 10% of requests) rather than a fixed count per call.
Store idempotency keys with the response and scope them per user/API key; replay the stored result on duplicate.

topics.title: Secure Python
topics.why: Python-specific footguns (pickle, yaml.load, subprocess shell=True, eval, tarfile extraction, XML) and the tools that catch them.

practices.text: Never unpickle or yaml.load untrusted data; use json or yaml.safe_load, and use defusedxml for XML from outside.
Run bandit (SAST) and pip-audit (SCA) in CI; both are Apache-2.0 and fast.

Install with --ignore-scripts in CI and enable the Node permission model (--permission) for tools that process untrusted input.

practices.text: Run govulncheck in CI; it only reports vulnerabilities in code paths you actually call, so it is low-noise.
Use os.Root (Go 1.24+) for any filesystem access rooted under a directory to stop path traversal and symlink escapes.

topics.title: Input validation and allowlisting
topics.why: First line of defence for every endpoint: schema-validate structure and type, allowlist values, reject rather than sanitise, and treat redirects/URLs as input too.

practices.text: Validate syntax then semantics with a schema library at the boundary; validation is a defence-in-depth layer, output encoding and parameterised queries are the primary injection controls.
For redirects, allowlist destinations or map to server-side IDs; never redirect to a user-supplied absolute URL.

topics.title: XSS prevention and output encoding
topics.why: Encode for the exact output context (HTML body, attribute, JS, URL, CSS), use framework auto-escaping, and lock down DOM sinks with Trusted Types.

practices.text: Use the template engine's auto-escaping and never build HTML by string concatenation; for DOM sinks (innerHTML, eval, setTimeout strings) enforce Trusted Types via CSP require-trusted-types-for.

resources.note: Context-by-context encoding rules; also read the DOM-based XSS sheet it links.

topics.title: HTML sanitisation of user content
topics.why: When you must render user-supplied rich text, use a maintained allowlist sanitiser; never regex-strip tags.

practices.text: Sanitise on output with DOMPurify (browser) or nh3/ammonia (Python/Rust) or OWASP Java HTML Sanitizer; sanitize-html and bleach are archived.

topics.title: CSRF protection
topics.why: State-changing requests need a CSRF defence: framework tokens, SameSite cookies, Fetch Metadata (Sec-Fetch-Site) or the stdlib middleware now available in Go.

practices.text: Prefer the framework's built-in CSRF middleware plus SameSite=Lax cookies; for APIs with bearer tokens CSRF is moot, for cookie-authenticated JSON APIs require a custom header and check Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site.

resources.name: justinas/nosurf (Go)
resources.note: Token-based middleware if you must support pre-1.25 Go or old browsers.

topics.title: SSRF prevention
topics.why: Any server-side fetch of a user-influenced URL must block internal ranges, resolve-then-connect to the same IP, disable redirects, and ideally go through an egress proxy.

practices.text: Allowlist destination hosts where possible; otherwise resolve DNS, reject private/link-local/metadata ranges (including IPv6 and 0.0.0.0), pin the resolved IP for the connection and cap redirects at zero.

resources.name: doyensec/safeurl (Go)
resources.note: Drop-in http.Client that blocks internal targets and DNS rebinding.

resources.name: y-mehta/ssrf-req-filter (Node)
resources.note: Small agent filter for axios/http; audit before use (tiny project).

resources.name: cujanovic/SSRF-Testing
resources.note: Bypass payloads (IP encodings, DNS tricks) to test your filter against.

resources.name: swisskyrepo/SSRFmap
resources.note: Offensive fuzzer; authorised scope only.

resources.name: FirstBuyer ssrf.ts: DNS-resolving, IP-pinned, redirect-guarded fetch for Node
resources.license_note: No LICENSE file in the repo; link only. The owner (AaroneGeorge) could add MIT to allow copying.
resources.note: 298 lines over undici. Also exports createGuardedFetch for handing a host-locked fetch to a payment wrapper. SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1 is a dev-only escape hatch: make sure it is unset in production. IPv6 allows only 2000::/3. Quality: Sound approach (resolve, pin the IP, manual redirects). No unit tests for the IP classifier; the repo's eval disables the guard. Compare with the libraries already in this topic before copying.

topics.title: SQL injection prevention and DB access control
topics.why: Parameterised queries everywhere, least-privilege DB roles, and knowing how attackers test (sqlmap) so you can verify the fix.

practices.text: Use prepared statements or the ORM parameter API for every query including ORDER BY and LIMIT (allowlist identifiers there); the DB user the app runs as must not own the schema or have superuser rights.

resources.name: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

resources.note: Transport encryption, account separation, least privilege for Postgres/MySQL/etc.

resources.name: sqlmapproject/sqlmap
resources.note: GPL-2.0 exploitation tool; run only against your own test instances to confirm a fix.

topics.title: OS command injection
topics.why: Shelling out with user data is still common in scripts and agents; use argv arrays, never shell strings, and prefer library calls over binaries.

practices.text: Call subprocess/execFile/exec.Command with an argument list and shell=False; if a shell is unavoidable, allowlist the argument and quote with shlex.quote or equivalent.

resources.name: OWASP OS Command Injection Defense Cheat Sheet
OWASP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
resources.note: Covers LDAP, XPath, NoSQL and log injection too.

resources.name: commixproject/commix
resources.note: GPL-3.0 command-injection exploitation tool; authorised testing only.

topics.title: Insecure deserialisation
topics.why: Native serialisation (Java, pickle, PHP, .NET BinaryFormatter, YAML) executes code on load; use data-only formats or allowlist filters and scan model/pickle files.

practices.text: Deserialise untrusted input only with data-only formats (JSON, protobuf); if Java serialization is unavoidable, use JEP 290 ObjectInputFilter allowlists; in Python never pickle.load untrusted bytes, scan with fickling.

resources.name: trailofbits/fickling
resources.note: Pickle decompiler and static analyzer; use to vet ML checkpoints and cached objects.

resources.name: frohoff/ysoserial
resources.note: Java gadget-chain payload generator; test harness for your filters, authorised use only.

topics.title: Path traversal and file access
topics.why: User-controlled file names must be confined to a root directory, with symlinks and ../ handled by the OS API, not by string checks.

practices.text: Confine access with os.Root (Go), a resolved-path prefix check after realpath (Python pathlib.resolve(strict)), or resolve-path (Node); generate server-side filenames instead of trusting client names.

resources.name: Go os.Root blog post
resources.note: Explains traversal, symlink races and how the kernel-backed API fixes them; concepts apply to every language.

resources.name: pillarjs/resolve-path (Node)

resources.note: Encodings and bypasses to include in tests.

topics.title: XML external entities and XML parser hardening
topics.why: Default XML parsers in many languages resolve external entities and DTDs; disable them or use hardened wrappers.

practices.text: Disable DTDs entirely (disallow-doctype-decl) on every XML parser; in Python route parsing through defusedxml; prefer JSON where you control the format.

resources.name: OWASP XXE Prevention Cheat Sheet
resources.note: Per-parser configuration snippets for Java, .NET, PHP, Python, C/C++.

resources.name: tiran/defusedxml
resources.note: PSF-licensed; finished and stable, still the standard Python answer.

topics.title: Secure file upload
topics.why: Uploads combine traversal, content-type spoofing, malware, image-parser bugs and storage DoS; validate by magic bytes, rename, store outside the web root, scan.

practices.text: Detect type by content (magic bytes) not extension or Content-Type, enforce size limits, store under a random server-generated name outside the web root or in object storage, and serve with Content-Disposition and a strict CSP.

resources.name: sindresorhus/file-type (JS)
resources.note: Magic-byte detection for buffers/streams.

resources.name: ahupp/python-magic
resources.note: libmagic binding (MIT); needs the libmagic system library.

resources.name: Cisco-Talos/clamav
resources.note: Run as a clamd sidecar and scan uploads asynchronously; GPL, used as a service not linked.

topics.title: IDOR, BOLA and mass assignment
topics.why: Broken object-level authorisation is the number-one API bug; every object fetch needs an ownership/permission check, and binders must allowlist fields.

practices.text: Check authorisation on every object access server-side using the session identity (not IDs from the client); bind request bodies to explicit DTOs/allowlists so clients cannot set role, owner or price fields.

resources.name: OWASP API Security Top 10 - API1 BOLA

topics.title: Prototype pollution (JavaScript)
topics.why: Merging untrusted objects into JS objects can set __proto__ and reach gadgets in libraries; freeze prototypes, use Map/null-prototype objects, and lint merges.

resources.name: OWASP Prototype Pollution Prevention Cheat Sheet
BlackFan/client-side-prototype-pollution
resources.note: Catalogue of gadgets in popular libraries; check your dependency list against it.

resources.name: PortSwigger prototype pollution labs
resources.note: Web Security Academy has a dedicated prototype pollution module with labs.

topics.title: ReDoS and regex safety
topics.why: Backtracking regexes on user input can hang a service; detect catastrophic patterns and use linear-time engines where possible.

practices.text: Lint regexes with recheck in CI; for user-controlled patterns or hot paths use a linear engine (RE2, Go regexp, Rust regex) and always bound input length.

resources.name: makenowjust-labs/recheck
resources.note: ReDoS checker with fuzzing plus automata analysis; ESLint plugin available.

resources.name: google/re2
resources.note: Guaranteed linear-time engine; bindings for Python (google-re2), Node (re2), Java.

resources.name: OWASP Denial of Service Cheat Sheet

topics.title: HTTP request smuggling, race conditions and cache attacks
topics.why: Protocol-level bugs between proxies and origins (desync, cache poisoning/deception) and limit-overrun races; mostly fixed by configuration and idempotent design.

practices.text: Use HTTP/2 end-to-end or normalise ambiguous requests at the edge, reject requests with both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding, and make state-changing operations idempotent with DB-level constraints to kill TOCTOU races.

resources.name: PortSwigger - Smashing the state machine (race conditions)
resources.note: Single-packet attack research; the definitive write-up on web race conditions.

resources.note: Apache-2.0 in-repo; authorised testing only.

resources.name: defparam/smuggler
resources.note: Standalone Python desync tester; unmaintained but still works.

topics.title: Server-side template injection
topics.why: Passing user input into template source (not template variables) gives RCE in Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker and friends; use sandboxed engines and never concatenate templates.

resources.name: PortSwigger SSTI learning path
resources.note: Server-side template injection module with per-engine exploitation and defence notes.

resources.name: epinna/tplmap
resources.note: Detection/exploitation tool; stale but useful for confirming fixes on test systems.

topics.title: GraphQL and API-specific hardening
topics.why: GraphQL adds introspection leaks, query depth/complexity DoS, batching brute force and field-level authz gaps on top of the usual API risks.

practices.text: Disable introspection in production, enforce depth and cost limits, use persisted queries where possible, and apply authorisation per field/resolver, not per endpoint.

resources.name: dolevf/graphql-cop
resources.note: Quick audit of a GraphQL endpoint for the common misconfigurations.

resources.name: nikitastupin/clairvoyance
resources.note: Recovers schema when introspection is off; shows why disabling introspection alone is not a control.

resources.name: OWASP Microservices Security Cheat Sheet
resources.note: Service-to-service authn/authz patterns (edge vs. per-service, token propagation).

topics.title: Password storage and strength (Argon2id, zxcvbn, breached-password checks)
topics.why: Hash passwords with Argon2id (bcrypt as fallback), check strength with zxcvbn and against breached-password lists instead of composition rules.

practices.text: Use Argon2id with at least m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1 (OWASP minimum) or bcrypt cost 10+ with a 72-byte pre-hash guard; store the parameters with the hash and rehash on login when they are below policy.
Follow NIST 800-63B: minimum 8 (ideally 15) characters, allow 64+, no forced rotation or composition rules, and block passwords found in breach corpora via the k-anonymity Pwned Passwords API.

resources.name: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet
resources.note: Current parameter recommendations for Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt, PBKDF2.

resources.name: hynek/argon2-cffi (Python)
resources.note: PasswordHasher class with sane defaults and check_needs_rehash.

resources.name: alexedwards/argon2id (Go)
resources.note: Thin wrapper around x/crypto/argon2 with PHC string encoding.

resources.note: Maintained TypeScript port of Dropbox zxcvbn (original last pushed 2024); use with the HIBP range API.

topics.title: Session management
topics.why: Server-side sessions with random IDs, secure cookie flags, rotation on login/privilege change, idle and absolute timeouts, and proper logout.

practices.text: Generate session IDs with a CSPRNG (128+ bits), set cookies with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and the __Host- prefix, rotate the ID on authentication, and invalidate server-side on logout.

resources.name: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet
resources.note: Login flow, error messages, re-authentication for sensitive actions.

resources.name: NIST SP 800-63-4 Digital Identity Guidelines
resources.note: Revision 4 (2025); 63B covers authenticators and session timeouts per assurance level.

resources.name: lucia-auth/lucia (learning resource)
resources.note: Now a guide (not a library) on implementing sessions yourself correctly in TypeScript.

topics.title: Multi-factor authentication (TOTP, recovery codes)
topics.why: Add TOTP (RFC 6238) with recovery codes and rate limits; avoid SMS; prefer passkeys when the audience allows.

practices.text: Store TOTP secrets encrypted, accept a +/-1 step window, reject reuse of a code, rate-limit attempts, and issue single-use hashed recovery codes.

resources.name: pyauth/pyotp
resources.note: MIT in-repo; HOTP/TOTP plus provisioning URIs.

topics.title: WebAuthn and passkeys
topics.why: Phishing-resistant authentication; use a server library that validates attestation/assertion properly and follow passkeys.dev UX guidance.

practices.text: Use a maintained server library, store credential IDs and sign counts, bind to your RP ID, and offer passkeys as the primary factor with a password or TOTP fallback only where needed.

resources.name: passkeys.dev
resources.note: FIDO Alliance / W3C community guidance, device support matrix, UX patterns.

resources.name: MasterKale/SimpleWebAuthn (TypeScript)
resources.note: Server + browser packages; the default choice for Node/Deno/Bun.

resources.name: kanidm/webauthn-rs
resources.note: Rust server library; webauthn4j is the Java equivalent.

topics.title: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect done safely
topics.why: Use the authorization-code flow with PKCE everywhere, follow RFC 9700 (OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice), and never roll your own token endpoint.

practices.text: Authorization code + PKCE for all clients (no implicit or password grants), exact redirect URI matching, state and nonce checked, short-lived access tokens with rotating refresh tokens, and sender-constrain tokens where possible.

resources.name: RFC 9700 - OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice
resources.note: Published Jan 2025; the authoritative threat-and-mitigation list.

resources.name: oauth.net
resources.note: Index of specs, OAuth 2.1 draft status and client libraries.

resources.name: authlib/authlib (Python)
resources.note: Client and server OAuth/OIDC/JOSE for Flask, Django, Starlette.

resources.name: ory/fosite (Go SDK)
resources.note: Security-first OAuth2/OIDC server SDK; powers ory/hydra.

topics.title: JWT and token handling
topics.why: Verify algorithm and key explicitly, keep tokens short-lived, store them out of reach of XSS, and consider PASETO or opaque tokens where JWT flexibility is not needed.

practices.text: Pin the expected alg and key per issuer (reject none and key-confusion), validate iss/aud/exp/nbf, keep access tokens minutes-lived, and never put secrets or PII in claims.

resources.name: RFC 8725 - JSON Web Token Best Current Practices
panva/jose (JS)

resources.name: paragonie/paseto

topics.title: Self-hosted identity providers and auth frameworks
topics.why: Instead of writing login, delegate to a maintained IdP (SSO, MFA, passkeys, OIDC) or a full-featured auth framework.

resources.name: keycloak/keycloak
resources.note: CNCF IdP; heavy (JVM) but the most complete OIDC/SAML server.

resources.name: goauthentik/authentik

resources.name: zitadel/zitadel
resources.note: Go IdP with multi-tenancy; AGPL.

resources.name: better-auth/better-auth
resources.note: TypeScript auth framework (passkeys, 2FA, orgs) embedded in your app; alternative to next-auth.

topics.title: Rate limiting, credential stuffing and account-recovery flows
topics.why: Brute force, credential stuffing, enumeration via error messages, and insecure password reset are the usual ways authentication fails in practice.

practices.text: Rate-limit by account and IP, return identical responses for unknown users, use single-use time-limited reset tokens sent out of band, and never implement security questions.

resources.name: OWASP Credential Stuffing Prevention Cheat Sheet
express-rate-limit
resources.note: Use a shared store (Redis) in multi-instance deployments.

topics.title: Service-to-service authentication (mTLS, SPIFFE, API keys)
topics.why: Machines need identities too: mutual TLS with short-lived certs, SPIFFE IDs, or hashed API keys with scopes and rotation.

practices.text: Store API keys hashed like passwords, show them once, scope and expire them, and prefer short-lived certificates (step-ca, SPIRE) or cloud workload identity over long-lived shared secrets.

topics.title: Authorisation design (RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC, deny by default)
topics.why: Broken access control is OWASP A01; centralise decisions, deny by default, check at the object level, and keep policy out of controllers.

practices.text: Enforce authorisation server-side in one place (middleware or policy engine), default deny, check on every request including object and field level, and log denials.

resources.name: OWASP Top 10:2025 A01 Broken Access Control
OWASP Transaction Authorization Cheat Sheet
resources.note: Step-up authorisation for high-value actions.

topics.why: Externalise policy into a tested engine instead of if-statements: OPA/Rego for infra and APIs, Cedar for app permissions, Casbin for embedded RBAC/ABAC, OpenFGA/SpiceDB for relationship graphs.

topics.title: Cryptographic right answers (what to use, what to avoid)
topics.why: Default choices for each need (encrypt, sign, hash, KDF, random, TLS) so an agent never picks an algorithm or mode itself.

practices.text: Symmetric: XChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-256-GCM via a high-level library; signatures: Ed25519; key exchange: X25519 (hybrid with ML-KEM for new designs); passwords: Argon2id; hashing: SHA-256/BLAKE2; random: the OS CSPRNG; never hand-roll modes or padding.

resources.name: Latacora - Cryptographic Right Answers, Post-Quantum Edition (2024)
resources.note: The current edition of the classic list; read this first.

resources.name: OWASP Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet
resources.note: Algorithm and key-size minimums plus storage patterns.

resources.name: Soatok - Why AES-GCM Sucks
resources.note: Nonce-misuse and limits explained; why XChaCha20-Poly1305 is the safer default.

resources.name: Practical Cryptography for Developers (free book)

topics.title: Misuse-resistant crypto libraries (libsodium/NaCl, Tink)
topics.why: High-level APIs that choose algorithms and nonces for you; the default when a project needs encryption or signatures.

practices.text: Use libsodium (crypto_secretbox / crypto_box / crypto_sign) or Tink AEAD/Signature primitives with keysets; do not touch OpenSSL EVP or raw primitives in application code.

topics.title: File encryption and signing tools (age, minisign)
topics.why: Encrypt files and backups or sign releases without GPG: age for encryption, minisign for signatures, both tiny and scriptable.

practices.text: Use age (or rage) with recipient public keys or SSH keys for file encryption; sign release artefacts with minisign or Sigstore rather than GPG.

topics.why: Which library to reach for in each language when libsodium is not an option: pyca/cryptography, RustCrypto/ring/rustls, Go x/crypto, OpenSSL/BoringSSL/AWS-LC.

topics.title: TLS server configuration and testing
topics.why: Pick a known-good cipher suite/protocol profile for nginx/Caddy/Apache/HAProxy and verify it with a scanner instead of hand-tuning.

practices.text: Use the Mozilla Intermediate profile (TLS 1.2+1.3, modern AEAD suites, HSTS) unless you need legacy clients; disable TLS 1.0/1.1, enable OCSP stapling, and re-scan after every config change.

resources.note: Modern/Intermediate/Old profiles with exact suite lists.

resources.name: testssl/testssl.sh
resources.note: Bash TLS scanner for any port; works offline against internal hosts.

resources.name: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

topics.title: Certificates, ACME and private PKI
topics.why: Automate public certs with ACME, run a private CA for internal TLS/mTLS/SSH, and use mkcert for local development.

practices.text: Automate renewal (certbot, lego, acme.sh or Caddy built-in), keep lifetimes short, and for internal services run step-ca instead of self-signed certs.

resources.note: Apache-2.0; the reference ACME client from EFF.

topics.title: Key management and encrypting data at rest
topics.why: Envelope encryption, rotation, separation of keys from data, and field/database-level encryption without inventing a scheme.

practices.text: Use envelope encryption (data keys wrapped by a KMS/Vault transit key), rotate wrapping keys on a schedule, never store keys beside ciphertext, and encrypt only the fields you must query less.

resources.note: Encryption-as-a-service and key rotation without exposing keys to the app.

topics.title: Post-quantum cryptography migration
topics.why: ML-KEM/ML-DSA (FIPS 203/204) are standardised and shipping in TLS; new designs should use hybrid key exchange and plan signature migration.

practices.text: Enable hybrid X25519+ML-KEM in TLS (default in Go 1.24+, OpenSSL 3.5, rustls/aws-lc, browsers) and inventory long-lived encrypted data first; do not deploy standalone PQ signatures in production yet without a reason.

topics.title: Secrets managers (OpenBao, Vault, Infisical)
topics.why: Central store with access control, audit log, dynamic credentials and rotation; apps fetch at runtime instead of baking secrets in.

practices.text: Apps should receive secrets at runtime via a short-lived identity (OIDC, AppRole, Kubernetes SA), never from committed files or long-lived tokens; enable audit logging and prefer dynamic DB credentials.

resources.note: Linux Foundation fork of Vault under MPL after the BUSL change; API compatible; the open-source default.

topics.title: Encrypted secrets in git and local dev (sops, age, dotenvx, gopass)
topics.why: For small deployments, encrypt secret files in the repo with sops+age and keep local .env files out of git; a secrets manager is not always needed.

practices.text: Commit only sops-encrypted YAML/JSON/.env (age or KMS keys), keep decrypted files in .gitignore, and give CI a dedicated age key or KMS role; rotate when a key holder leaves.

topics.title: Secret detection in code and history
topics.why: Catch committed credentials before push (pre-commit) and in CI, and scan history and containers for leaks.

practices.text: Run gitleaks (or trufflehog) as a pre-commit hook and in CI on every PR, enable GitHub push protection, and treat any hit as compromised: rotate first, then clean history.

topics.why: What to do in the first hour: revoke and rotate, find usage, purge history, and add detection so it does not recur.

practices.text: Rotate the credential immediately (assume it was harvested within minutes of the push), audit its usage logs, then rewrite history with git-filter-repo and force-push only after everyone has pulled; add the pattern to your scanner.

topics.title: Automated dependency updates (Renovate, Dependabot)
topics.why: Keep dependencies current with grouped, tested PRs and a release cooldown so you are neither months behind nor first to install a compromised version.

practices.text: Use Renovate with minimumReleaseAge of 3-7 days, group minor/patch updates, pin digests for Docker and GitHub Actions, and enable vulnerability alerts so security fixes skip the cooldown.

topics.title: Lockfile hygiene, install scripts and release cooldowns
topics.why: The 2025 npm worm attacks (chalk/debug, Shai-Hulud, nx) spread via install scripts and fresh releases; frozen lockfiles, --ignore-scripts and a minimum release age block most of them.

practices.text: Always install from the lockfile in CI (npm ci, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, uv sync --locked, cargo --locked), set ignore-scripts=true for npm/pnpm, and configure pnpm minimumReleaseAge (or npm --before) to 1-7 days.
Lint lockfiles for non-registry URLs and hash drift (lockfile-lint) and review lockfile diffs in PRs like code.

topics.why: Prevent account-takeover publishing of your own packages: OIDC trusted publishing from CI, mandatory 2FA, and provenance attestations on npm/PyPI.

practices.text: Publish only from CI via trusted publishing (PyPI, npm, RubyGems, crates.io) with no long-lived tokens, require 2FA on all maintainers, and enable provenance so consumers can verify the build.

resources.name: npm Trusted Publishers
resources.note: OIDC publishing with automatic provenance; classic tokens were deprecated after the 2025 attacks.

resources.name: sigstore/sigstore-python
resources.note: Apache-2.0; sign and verify Python artefacts; used by the pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish attestations.

resources.name: ossf/wg-securing-software-repos
resources.note: Principles for Package Repository Security; what registries should (and now do) enforce.

topics.title: Semgrep / Opengrep pattern-based SAST
topics.why: Fast multi-language SAST with readable rules; write project-specific rules to enforce secure patterns. Note the rules licence.

practices.text: Run semgrep with p/default or language packs in CI (SARIF to code scanning), add a repo-local .semgrep/ folder of custom rules for your own secure wrappers, and keep the Semgrep Rules License in mind (internal use only, no redistribution as a service).

resources.name: semgrep/semgrep
resources.note: Engine is LGPL; CE registry rules are under the Semgrep Rules License v1.0 (not OSI). The semgrep mcp subcommand is built in.

resources.name: semgrep/semgrep-rules
resources.note: Semgrep Rules License v1.0: free internal use, no redistribution or SaaS; do not vendor into a shared product.

resources.name: opengrep/opengrep
resources.note: Community fork (2025) after the rules relicensing; CLI-compatible, rules under permissive licences.

resources.name: trailofbits/semgrep-rules
resources.note: High-signal rules (Python, Go, Rust, JS); AGPL, use via registry p/trailofbits.

resources.name: 0xdea/semgrep-rules
resources.note: MIT rules for C/C++ vulnerability research; safe to vendor.

topics.title: CodeQL semantic analysis
topics.why: Dataflow-based SAST with the deepest taint tracking for Java, C/C++, C#, Go, JS/TS, Python, Ruby, Swift, Kotlin, Rust; free for public repos via code scanning.

practices.text: Enable default code scanning on every public repo (free), use the security-extended query suite, and triage alerts in PR instead of batch; for private repos the CLI is free for research but requires GHAS for CI use.

resources.name: github/codeql
resources.note: Query libraries are MIT; the CLI binary has its own terms (free for OSS/research).

resources.name: github/securitylab
resources.note: Research queries and the CodeQL bug-bounty corpus; good examples for writing custom queries.

resources.name: trailofbits/skills - static-analysis
resources.note: Agent skill for running CodeQL/Semgrep and reading SARIF; runs local tooling.

topics.title: Dependency vulnerability scanners (osv-scanner, Trivy, Grype, dependency-check)
topics.why: Find known CVEs in lockfiles, SBOMs, containers and filesystems; pick one primary scanner and run it on every PR and nightly.

practices.text: Run osv-scanner (lockfiles, call-graph aware for Go/Rust) or trivy fs in PRs, scan built images nightly, and suppress with VEX statements in the repo rather than ignoring whole packages.

resources.name: google/osv-scanner
resources.note: OSV-backed, supports guided remediation and licence scanning; lowest false-positive rate for lockfiles.

resources.name: aquasecurity/trivy
resources.note: One binary for deps, images, IaC, secrets, SBOM, Kubernetes; the default all-in-one.

resources.name: anchore/grype
resources.note: Scans syft SBOMs; strong offline/air-gapped DB workflow.

resources.name: dependency-check/DependencyCheck
resources.note: OWASP; strongest for JVM/.NET builds; needs an NVD API key for fast DB updates.

resources.name: RetireJS/retire.js
resources.note: Detects vulnerable front-end JS libraries in bundles and pages.

topics.title: Dynamic web scanning (ZAP, Nuclei, Nikto, Wapiti)
topics.why: Black-box scan a running app or staging site for misconfigurations and common vulns; ZAP for apps, Nuclei for templated checks across hosts.

practices.text: Run ZAP baseline scan in CI against ephemeral environments and nuclei with the http/misconfiguration and exposures templates against your own hosts; both only on systems you own or have written permission for.

resources.name: zaproxy/zaproxy
resources.note: The open-source DAST and proxy; automation framework and Docker images for CI.

resources.name: zaproxy/action-full-scan
resources.note: Also action-baseline and action-api-scan for lighter CI runs.

resources.name: projectdiscovery/nuclei
resources.note: YAML template engine; fast and scriptable; needs network to the target.

resources.name: projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates
resources.note: 10k+ community templates (CVEs, misconfigs, exposures); mirror for offline scanning.

resources.name: wapiti-scanner/wapiti
resources.note: Python black-box scanner; lighter than ZAP, GPL.

topics.why: Generate requests from an OpenAPI/GraphQL schema to find 500s, schema violations and auth gaps automatically.

resources.name: akto-api-security/akto
resources.note: API inventory and testing platform (now also MCP/agent testing); heavier self-hosted stack.

topics.title: IaC and Kubernetes manifest scanning (Checkov, KICS, Trivy, kube-linter)
topics.why: Catch misconfigurations in Terraform, CloudFormation, Helm, Kubernetes YAML and Compose before deploy.

practices.text: Run trivy config or checkov on every IaC change, fail on HIGH+, and encode exceptions as inline skip comments with a reason; terrascan is archived.

resources.name: bridgecrewio/checkov
resources.note: Broadest policy coverage (Terraform, CFN, K8s, Helm, Dockerfile, GitHub Actions).

resources.name: aquasecurity/trivy (config scanning)

resources.name: stackrox/kube-linter

topics.why: Lint Dockerfiles for bad practice, scan built images for OS and app CVEs, and check image configuration (root user, exposed secrets).

resources.name: quay/clair
resources.note: Registry-integrated scanner service; use when running your own registry.

topics.why: Run many scanners consistently and aggregate results into one place with deduplication and SLAs.

resources.note: Runs 100+ linters including security ones; AGPL tool, fine as CI step.

topics.title: Coverage-guided fuzzing for C/C++ (AFL++, libFuzzer, honggfuzz, LibAFL)
topics.why: Find memory-safety and parsing bugs in native code automatically; write a small harness, build with sanitizers, run for hours.

practices.text: Write LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput harnesses (they run under libFuzzer, AFL++ and honggfuzz), compile with ASan+UBSan, seed with real inputs and a dictionary, and commit the corpus; minimise and triage crashes before fixing.

resources.name: AFLplusplus/AFLplusplus
resources.note: Best general-purpose fuzzer; AGPL applies to the fuzzer, not your target; QEMU mode for binaries.

resources.name: AFLplusplus/LibAFL

topics.title: Fuzzing Rust (cargo-fuzz, afl.rs, arbitrary)
topics.why: Rust panics, overflows and unsafe blocks are fuzzable in minutes with cargo-fuzz; structured inputs via arbitrary.

practices.text: Add a fuzz/ crate with cargo fuzz init, derive Arbitrary for structured inputs, run under ASan nightly, and keep fuzz targets in CI (short runs) plus OSS-Fuzz or ClusterFuzzLite for long runs.

resources.name: rust-fuzz/trophy-case
resources.note: Bugs found by fuzzing Rust crates; motivation and examples of what to look for.

topics.title: Fuzzing Go, Python, JVM and Node (native go fuzz, Atheris, Jazzer)
topics.why: Managed languages still have panics, DoS, logic and injection bugs; built-in Go fuzzing and Jazzer/Atheris make harnesses cheap.

resources.note: go test -fuzz built into the toolchain since 1.18; corpus lives in testdata/fuzz.

resources.note: libFuzzer for Python with coverage of native extensions.

resources.note: JVM fuzzer with JUnit integration and sanitizers for deserialization, injection, SSRF.

resources.name: CodeIntelligenceTesting/jazzer.js
resources.note: Node fuzzer with Jest integration and prototype-pollution bug detectors.

resources.name: trailofbits/ruzzy
resources.note: Ruby fuzzer; niche.

topics.title: Continuous fuzzing (OSS-Fuzz, ClusterFuzzLite, fuzz-introspector)
topics.why: Fuzzing finds bugs over time; run it continuously in CI or get free infrastructure as an open-source project.

practices.text: Add ClusterFuzzLite to CI for PR-time fuzzing of changed code, apply to OSS-Fuzz if the project is widely used, and use fuzz-introspector reports to see which code the harnesses never reach.

resources.name: google/oss-fuzz
resources.note: Free continuous fuzzing for critical OSS; the projects/ folder holds thousands of example build scripts and harnesses to copy.

resources.name: google/clusterfuzzlite
resources.note: OSS-Fuzz in your own GitHub Actions/GitLab CI.

resources.name: google/oss-fuzz-gen
resources.note: LLM-generated fuzz harnesses; study its prompts when asking an agent to write harnesses. Needs model API keys.

resources.name: google/syzkaller
resources.note: Kernel syscall fuzzer; only for OS/driver work.

topics.why: Tutorials to get a first fuzzer running and tools for stateful network protocol targets.

resources.name: trailofbits/skills - testing-handbook-skills

topics.title: Linux server hardening baseline
topics.why: The checklist for any new Ubuntu/Debian host: users and sudo, SSH, firewall, automatic updates, sysctl, auditd, kernel options, minimal services.

practices.text: Non-root user with key-only SSH, ufw/nftables default deny with only Tailscale/SSH open, unattended-upgrades for security patches, auditd on, and run lynis audit system after changes.

resources.name: imthenachoman/How-To-Secure-A-Linux-Server
resources.note: Practical, Debian/Ubuntu-oriented, maintained; the single best home-server guide.

resources.name: CISOfy/lynis
resources.note: Agentless audit with a hardening index; GPL, run as a tool.

resources.note: Deep, opinionated (kernel params, sysctl, boot flags); pick what fits a server.

resources.name: a13xp0p0v/kernel-hardening-checker
resources.note: Checks kernel config, cmdline and sysctl against KSPP recommendations.

resources.name: trimstray/the-practical-linux-hardening-guide
resources.note: RHEL-leaning, slow-moving but thorough (partitions, PAM, SELinux).

topics.why: Apply and audit a recognised baseline automatically instead of hand-editing configs.

resources.note: Free PDFs after registration; the baseline most tools below implement.

resources.name: aquasecurity/kube-bench
resources.note: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark checks.

topics.title: SSH hardening
topics.why: Key-only auth, modern algorithms, no root login, and certificates or Tailscale SSH for access management.

practices.text: PasswordAuthentication no, PermitRootLogin no, modern KEX/cipher/MAC set from the Mozilla guide, AllowUsers/AllowGroups, and audit with ssh-audit after each change; consider SSH certificates via step-ca.

resources.name: jtesta/ssh-audit
resources.note: Audits server and client algorithms; includes hardening guides per distro in its docs.

topics.title: systemd service sandboxing
topics.why: Every service unit can be confined (ProtectSystem, PrivateTmp, NoNewPrivileges, CapabilityBoundingSet, SystemCallFilter) with a few lines; systemd-analyze security scores it.

practices.text: Start with DynamicUser=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, NoNewPrivileges=yes, RestrictAddressFamilies, SystemCallFilter=@system-service, then iterate until systemd-analyze security <unit> is below 3 without breaking the service.

resources.name: systemd.exec man page
resources.note: Authoritative list of sandboxing directives.

resources.name: ctrl.blog - systemd service hardening guide
resources.note: Walkthrough of systemd-analyze security and the directives that matter.

resources.name: alegrey91/systemd-service-hardening
resources.note: Old but concise directive-by-directive explanation.

topics.title: Brute-force and intrusion prevention (fail2ban, CrowdSec)
topics.why: Ban hosts that fail authentication or hit scanners; CrowdSec adds a crowd-sourced blocklist and WAF component.

resources.name: crowdsecurity/crowdsec
resources.note: Parses logs from SSH, nginx, Caddy, Traefik, Docker; bouncers for firewall and proxies; community blocklist needs outbound network.

resources.name: fail2ban/fail2ban
resources.note: GPL-2.0; simple and local-only; still fine for SSH on a single host.

resources.name: OWASP Credential Stuffing Prevention Cheat Sheet

topics.title: Process sandboxing on Linux (bubblewrap, firejail, nsjail, Landlock)
topics.why: Confine a single untrusted process (parsers, converters, agent tool calls) with namespaces, seccomp and Landlock without a full container.

practices.text: For one-off untrusted commands use bubblewrap with --unshare-all, read-only binds of only what is needed and a seccomp filter; for long-running tools use systemd sandboxing; Landlock for in-process self-restriction.

resources.name: containers/bubblewrap
resources.note: LGPL-2.0; unprivileged, used by Flatpak and by anthropics/sandbox-runtime on Linux.

resources.name: google/nsjail
resources.note: Namespaces + cgroups + seccomp with a config file; common for CTF and code-execution services.

resources.name: netblue30/firejail
resources.note: Desktop-oriented profiles for hundreds of apps; setuid design, so review before servers.

resources.name: Landlock kernel documentation
resources.note: Unprivileged filesystem/network access-control LSM in mainline; rust-landlock and Go bindings exist.

topics.title: Docker and Compose hardening
topics.why: Run containers as non-root, drop capabilities, read-only root, no-new-privileges, no Docker socket mounts, rootless daemon where possible.

practices.text: In Compose set user, read_only: true, cap_drop: [ALL], security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true], tmpfs for writable paths, resource limits, and never mount /var/run/docker.sock into a container that faces the network.

resources.name: OWASP Docker Security Cheat Sheet
resources.note: Rules 0-12; the practical checklist.

resources.name: Rootless Docker
resources.note: Daemon as unprivileged user; limits damage from container escapes.

resources.name: docker/docker-bench-security
resources.note: CIS Docker Benchmark checks for host and daemon.

resources.name: OWASP Docker Top 10
resources.note: Finished guide to the ten container risks; still accurate.

topics.title: Stronger container isolation (gVisor, Kata, Firecracker, Sysbox)
topics.why: When a container runs untrusted code (CI jobs, user plugins, agents) the shared kernel is the risk; use a user-space kernel or microVM runtime.

resources.name: google/gvisor
resources.note: runsc runtime drop-in for Docker/containerd; intercepts syscalls; modest overhead.

resources.name: firecracker-microvm/firecracker
resources.note: MicroVMs with ~125ms boot; backs Lambda, Fly.io, E2B; needs KVM.

resources.name: kata-containers/kata-containers
resources.note: OCI-compatible VM-per-pod runtime for Kubernetes.

resources.name: nestybox/sysbox
resources.note: Run Docker-in-Docker or systemd inside unprivileged containers.

topics.title: Kubernetes cluster hardening
topics.why: Pod Security Standards, RBAC least privilege, network policies, secrets encryption, admission control, and posture scanning.

practices.text: Enforce the restricted Pod Security Standard per namespace, default-deny NetworkPolicies, no cluster-admin for workloads, encrypt Secrets at rest, and scan with kubescape or kube-bench on a schedule.

resources.name: kubescape/kubescape
resources.note: CNCF; scans clusters/manifests against NSA-CISA, MITRE, CIS frameworks.

topics.why: Block bad manifests at admission and detect suspicious behaviour at runtime with eBPF.

resources.name: open-policy-agent/gatekeeper
resources.note: OPA/Rego-based; pick if you already use OPA elsewhere.

resources.name: falcosecurity/falco

resources.name: cilium/tetragon

resources.name: kubearmor/KubeArmor

topics.why: Audit AWS/Azure/GCP accounts against CIS and well-architected baselines; remediate drift with policy.

practices.text: Run prowler against every account on a schedule with the CIS and well-architected checks, fix public buckets, root MFA, logging and IAM first, and use cloud-custodian policies to prevent recurrence.

resources.name: prowler-cloud/prowler
resources.note: AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, M365; hundreds of checks mapped to frameworks; needs cloud read credentials.

resources.name: cloud-custodian/cloud-custodian

resources.note: Write least-privilege AWS policies from a short YAML of resources and access levels.

resources.name: salesforce/cloudsplaining
resources.note: Audits existing AWS IAM for privilege escalation and data exfiltration paths.

topics.title: Web application firewalls (Coraza, ModSecurity + CRS, BunkerWeb, SafeLine)
topics.why: A virtual patch layer in front of self-hosted apps; the OWASP Core Rule Set is the detection logic, Coraza/ModSecurity the engines.

practices.text: Deploy CRS at paranoia level 1 in detection-only mode first, tune false positives for a week, then block; a WAF is defence in depth, not a substitute for fixing the app.

resources.note: Go WAF engine, ModSecurity-compatible; Caddy and Traefik plugins exist.

resources.note: Now maintained under OWASP after Trustwave handed it over; nginx/Apache connector.

resources.name: bunkerity/bunkerweb
resources.note: Batteries-included nginx + CRS + bot protection; AGPL.

resources.name: chaitin/SafeLine

topics.title: Remote access and zero-trust networking (Tailscale ACLs, SSO proxies, Teleport)
topics.why: Keep services off the public internet: overlay network with ACLs, SSO in front of web apps, certificate-based SSH.

practices.text: Expose nothing publicly; reach services over Tailscale with explicit ACL grants per user/tag, put authelia or oauth2-proxy in front of any web UI without its own SSO, and use Tailscale SSH or SSH certificates instead of shared keys.

resources.name: gravitational/teleport

topics.title: HTTP security headers
topics.why: HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP/COEP/CORP: set them from one middleware and verify with a scanner.

practices.text: Use helmet (Node), secure (Python), unrolled/secure (Go) or the proxy to set the OWASP Secure Headers recommended set, then check with the MDN Observatory; add HSTS with preload only when all subdomains are HTTPS.

resources.name: OWASP Secure Headers Project
resources.note: Best-practice header values plus a JSON file of recommended headers to vendor; repo OWASP/secure-headers-project.

resources.name: TypeError/secure (Python)
resources.note: ASGI/WSGI middleware with presets for FastAPI, Django, Flask.

resources.name: MDN HTTP Observatory
resources.note: Successor to Mozilla Observatory (repo archived); scores headers and TLS; securityheaders.com is the alternative.

topics.title: Content Security Policy
topics.why: The strongest XSS mitigation: a nonce- or hash-based strict CSP with no unsafe-inline, plus Trusted Types for DOM sinks.

practices.text: Deploy a strict CSP (script-src 'nonce-...' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none') in report-only first, fix violations, then enforce; avoid allowlists of CDN hosts, they are bypassable.

CSP Evaluator
resources.note: Paste a policy, get bypass warnings; library at google/csp-evaluator.

topics.title: CORS configuration
topics.why: Misconfigured CORS (reflecting Origin with credentials, null origin, regex mistakes) turns an API into a cross-site data leak.

practices.text: Allowlist exact origins (never reflect the request Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true), do not allow the null origin, keep preflight caching short, and remember CORS is not an access control.

resources.name: expressjs/cors
resources.note: Pass an explicit origin array or function; the default allows all origins.

topics.title: Cookie security and client-side storage
topics.why: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, __Host- prefix, scoping and expiry; and why tokens do not belong in localStorage.

practices.text: Session cookies: Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (Strict for admin); Path=/; name prefixed __Host-; no Domain attribute; never store bearer tokens in localStorage where any XSS can read them.

resources.name: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet (cookie attributes)

practices.text: Draw a data-flow diagram with trust boundaries, enumerate threats per element with STRIDE, record mitigations as backlog items, and revisit the model whenever the architecture changes; keep it lightweight and continuous.

topics.title: Prompt injection defences and agent design patterns
topics.why: There is no filter that stops prompt injection; mitigate by architecture: avoid the lethal trifecta, constrain tool use, separate control from data, and verify actions.

practices.text: Never give one agent all three of: access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and a channel to exfiltrate; break the trifecta by removing one, e.g. no network egress or no untrusted input in the same context.
Apply the six design patterns (action-selector, plan-then-execute, map-reduce, dual LLM, code-then-execute, context minimisation) so untrusted text can never choose which privileged action runs.

resources.name: Zstandard
resources.note: Default fast compressor with dictionaries; lz4 (same author) when speed beats ratio.

resources.note: Instrumentation and sampling (AutoFDO) PGO for C/C++.

resources.name: cargo-pgo

resources.name: min-sized-rust

resources.name: aya

topics.title: Bash strict mode, pitfalls and error handling
topics.why: Writing Bash that fails loudly and correctly; knowing the traps of set -e, word splitting and subshells.

practices.text: Start scripts with `set -Eeuo pipefail` and understand its limits (command lists, pipelines, subshells).
Quote every expansion ("$var", "${arr[@]}"); use [[ ]] for tests and $(...) for substitution.
Use `trap cleanup EXIT` with mktemp -d for temp files; check `command -v tool` not `which`.
Prefer printf over echo; never parse ls output; iterate with globs or `find -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d ''`.

resources.name: FirstBuyer: x402 seller compliance checker with 13 failure fixtures and an eval matrix
resources.license_note: No LICENSE file in the repo; link only. The owner (AaroneGeorge) could add MIT to allow copying.
resources.note: Express 5 on Vercel, OKX x402 packages, viem. src/core/checks.ts is pure; test/fixtures.ts boots 13 deliberately broken sellers; eval/run.ts asserts outcomes with payment and buyer mocked. The README's Invariants section is worth reading. X Layer / USDT0 constants. Quality: Good separation (pure checks, guarded fetch, breaker, deadline). The eval runs with SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1, so the SSRF guard itself is not exercised by the matrix. Hot-wallet design documented; keys only via env.

resources.name: Ouroboros Press: ownerless contract that pays an agent swarm per job (Foundry)
resources.note: Solidity 0.8.26 + OpenZeppelin, Foundry. No owner, upgrade, pause or withdraw by construction. 32 unit + 3 fork tests: reentrancy through a malicious counterparty mock, callback under a 200k gas stipend, cool-down doubling, fuzzed JSON body. THREAT-MODEL.md and keystore-first ops scripts included. Chain constants (Robinhood Chain 4663, IMD Intake v2) are hard-coded by design. Quality: High: tests cover the stated invariants; the threat model says what is impossible and why. scripts/lib.sh has a machine-specific ENV_FILE default; fork tests need a live RPC.

resources.name: Warden: x402 spend-control proxy for agents (policy engine, Merkle receipts, anchor contracts)
resources.license_note: No LICENSE file in the repo; link only. The owner (AaroneGeorge) could add MIT to allow copying.
resources.note: Next.js 16 + viem; Foundry contracts (ReceiptAnchor, PolicyRegistry, 11 tests); 16 TS unit tests for the pure policy engine and the Merkle code; agent client in apps/agent; default WARDEN_SETTLE_MODE=simulated. Hackathon build on Arc testnet. Quality: The policy engine (apps/web/src/lib/policy.ts) is pure and well tested. Merkle leaves are single-hashed sorted pairs, not the OZ double-hashed leaf format: fine for receipts, do not reuse for airdrops. In-memory store; shared demo instance.
